level: Agent fs_write integration of the Linux descriptor-pinned brand-new-file publication path
componentAcceptance: verified on three platforms; the Linux publish path is the pinned component, the Windows path is unchanged, and the public fs_write contract is preserved
productAcceptance: partial; existing-target hash overwrite stays disabled on Linux, external-writer CAS and permissions work remain open
implementation: write() splits per platform after the unchanged argument validation, target resolution and in-flight target mutex: Linux publishes through pinnedCreateNewFile, every other platform keeps the legacy rename path byte-for-byte

Linux contract preservation: an existing target with expectedHash:null answers TARGET_EXISTS mapped to the public FILE_CHANGED; a matching hash on an existing target is refused OVERWRITE_UNSUPPORTED 501 instead of falling back to rename; a mismatched expectation and a missing target keep FILE_CHANGED, and FILE_TOO_LARGE is preserved

The admission WorkspacePin's real root is the pinned-create root. A pinnedWritePolicy hook rechecks grant validity, protected paths (assertPublicTree) and the pinned root identity at every component phase; an after-publish policy refusal becomes PINNED_WRITE_UNVERIFIED published:true, which the existing exception summary already maps to unknown with no stop proof and a retained lock

Pre-publication cancellation keeps possiblyApplied:false; post-publication cancellation keeps conservative effects with the shape-checked digest; both flow through the unchanged E66 summary and stop-receipt machinery

The existing final-pre-publication cancellation barrier in workspace-agent.native.mjs is re-anchored per publish path (legacy roots.read re-check vs pinned before-publish policy) without weakening any E66 assertion

New Linux-only Agent suite covers exact bytes/0600/one-link publication, existing-target and overwrite refusals, parent replacement while parked, an external creator winning the target, after-publish policy refusal (unknown + retained lock + reconciliation release) and after-publish cancellation with digest; the component suite and the new Agent suite enter npm test and thereby Windows/Ubuntu CI

platforms.combined: 71/71 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, exit 0 (pinned-write 27, workspace-agent-pinned 6, workspace-agent 8, workspace-generation 5, remote-write-tasks 14, task-retry-stop-evidence 11; identity/admission files contribute no tests in this fixture)

platforms.rootRegression: 1814 tests, 1760 pass, 0 fail, 54 skipped, exit 0 (log: tmp/integration/pinned-wiring-root-regression-final.log); Windows keeps the legacy publish path

preservedFailures: The first Ubuntu run failed 4 of 71: a remote-write CAS case expected FILE_CHANGED and received OVERWRITE_UNSUPPORTED (the wiring initially refused every expectedHash!==null request; fixed by refusing only a matching hash and keeping the CAS-refusal contract), and three new-fixture issues (parent replacement is detected by the admission pin's WORKSPACE_CHANGED before the component's DIRECTORY_CHANGED; an unscoped policy patch poisoned a follow-up write; a barrier release typo). The first Win10 run failed 5 of 8 files at load because the fixture lacked pinned-write.ts. None of these were silenced; each was fixed and rerun to green.
limitations: Existing-target overwrite stays disabled on Linux until a separately verified external-writer CAS and metadata contract exists; Windows publication keeps path-based rename semantics and gains no descriptor claims.

The pinned component's known boundaries carry over unchanged: inode pinning is not mount/security-label confinement, link() still resolves /proc/fd path strings, nlink is a single post-settlement observation.

Host-side remote-write surfaces, permissions/config generations beyond the Agent digest, cross-Agent dataDir coordination, container UID65532 real ownership, command/CLI write facades and full Task acceptance remain open.
